title: Hybrid rendezvous rate scheduler with graceful congestion fallback
creator: Ayesha Patel
description: Design and implement a hybrid routing and admission-control component for Dedicated fleets that combines rendezvous hashing-based routing, per-tenant soft rate reservations, a short in-memory queueing layer, and a graceful congestion fallback path that defers non-critical requests or routes them to lower-cost model variants. The goal is to provide predictable throughput guarantees for committed tenants while preserving low tail latency for latency-sensitive traffic and minimizing wasted GPU cycles during transient overloads.
acceptance_criteria: Committed tenants receive >= 95% of their reserved throughput under typical burst patterns (10x baseline) without manual intervention
95th percentile generation latency for high-priority lanes does not regress by more than 15ms in steady state after rollout
Under fleet-wide overload, non-critical work is deferred or routed to fallbacks with failure rate < 2% and bounded deferral window (configurable, default 60s)
New scheduler supports pluggable policy: rate cap, soft reservation, defer, and fallback routing, configurable per-tenant and per-model
End-to-end integration tests and canary in staging validate routing correctness and graceful degradation behavior
proposal: Introduce a centralized hybrid rendezvous rate scheduler (HRRS) in the Dedicated control plane. HRRS will: (1) use rendezvous hashing to map requests to a small set of candidate worker islands to maintain cache locality; (2) maintain lightweight in-memory soft reservations per tenant with a replenishing token window; (3) provide a short hop queue (per-worker, fixed-size, FIFO with priority lanes) to absorb microbursts; (4) when queueing cannot satisfy demand, trigger a graceful fallback: first attempt model-variant fallback (quantized or distilled), second attempt deferred execution (enqueue for delayed retry with callback), third attempt preemptible best-effort eviction. All steps are observable and configurable via the fleet policy API.
technical_approach: Routing: implement rendezvous hashing with a small candidate set (k=3) to reduce KV cache misses and keep shard affinity stable during rebalances
Reservations: token-bucket-like soft reservation per tenant with configurable refill rate and burst headroom; stored in control plane with approx. LRU eviction for sparse tenants

Queueing: per-worker in-process circular buffer with 3 priority lanes (high/normal/low). High lane bypasses queue when tokens exist. Low lane requests become eligible for deferral if occupancy thresholds exceed configured headroom

Fallbacks: model variant registry maps canonical models to compatible lower-cost variants. Deferred execution uses a lightweight callback URL or websocket reservation token for server-side retry up to N seconds
Backpressure signals: worker nodes emit occupancy and queue depth metrics; HRRS uses these to adjust soft admission thresholds via a simple proportional controller
Safety: introduce a circuit breaker to disable deferral/fallback per-tenant if errors spike; provide observability hooks and audit logs for every fallback decision
milestones: M1: Design doc + simulation harness (2 weeks)
M2: Rendezvous router + token reservation prototype (3 weeks)
M3: Worker queue and fallback APIs implemented (3 weeks)
M4: Staging canary with synthetic burst tests and integration with autoscaler (2 weeks)
M5: Gradual production rollout behind feature flag and operator dashboard (2 weeks)
M6: Post-rollout tuning and runbook updates (2 weeks)
metrics: Committed throughput fulfillment: percent of tenant reserved qps satisfied (per-tenant, per-1m)
Fallback usage breakdown: model-variant vs deferred vs preempted
Cost delta: GPU-seconds per delivered token compared to baseline
rollout_plan: Feature flagged rollout starting with internal Dedicated pools and low-risk tenants
Phase 1: 10% of traffic, monitor key metrics for 48h
Phase 2: 50% traffic if metrics stable for 72h, enable adaptive parameter tuning in staging
Phase 3: 100% traffic with operator override and automated rollback triggers
Include a manual kill-switch to revert to legacy routing/admission within 5 minutes
tests: Unit tests for rendezvous hash mapping and deterministic shard selection
Load tests with synthetic tenant mix (90th/95th/99th percentile burst patterns)
Chaos injection: kill worker nodes during bursts and validate fallback correctness
Integration test that simulates model-variant fallback compatibility mismatches
End-to-end latency regression test against production traffic sample
risks: If rendezvous candidate set is too small we may amplify hot-shard CPU/GPU pressure; too large and KV cache locality degrades
Deferred execution introduces complexity around idempotency, billing, and client semantics
Model-variant fallbacks may produce lower-quality outputs and require clear SLAs and customer opt-outs
Control plane failure modes could incorrectly compute reservations leading to tenant QoS violations
dependencies: runtime-1.18 (for worker-side queue and telemetry hooks)
